about: A football team that never wins

lines.text: Our school football team has not won a single match in two years.
Most people would have gave up by now, but our players turn up
lines.note: Verb form: after 'would have' it is 'given', not 'gave'.

lines.text: for training every Tuesday and Thursday without fail. The captain is a quiet
boy which never shouts, yet everyone listens when he speaks. Last month, we
lines.note: 'Which' is for things. A boy takes 'who'.

lines.text: lost by six goals to a team from a neighbouring school. Nobody cry
lines.note: Tense: the match was last month, so it is 'cried'.

lines.text: or blamed the goalkeeper. Instead, the players shook hands with his opponents and
lines.note: Pronoun: 'the players' is plural, so it is 'their'.

lines.text: stayed behind to practise passing. Our coach says that losing teach us things
lines.note: Agreement: 'losing' is one thing, so it is 'teaches'.

lines.text: that winning never could. We have learnt to be patience, to trust one
lines.note: Word form: after 'to be' an adjective is needed — 'patient'.

lines.text: another and to keep running until the whistle. We are also much fit than
we were two years ago. A few classmates laugh at our results, but
they have never watched us train. Whatever the score, I am proud with
this team, and I would not exchange it for any other.
